binaries.name: bdeinfo
binaries.why: Read a BitLocker volume header and the key protectors it can interpret, before any key is known. What it lists is what the installed build parsed for that metadata version; say which. No macOS install route is declared.

binaries.name: bdemount
binaries.why: Expose an unlocked BitLocker volume as a FUSE view. A mount lives in that VM only and is not a sealed output; materialise the volume or the scoped files under $OUT. FUSE may be unavailable in a worker, and no macOS install route is declared.

binaries.name: dislocker
binaries.why: Present a BitLocker volume through FUSE once a recovery password, a key file or a clear key is supplied. A mount lives in that VM only and is not a sealed output; FUSE may be unavailable in a worker. The recovery password is a command-line option: say so in the report, so the trace can be redacted.

binaries.name: cryptsetup
binaries.why: Read a LUKS header (luksDump: version, UUID, data offset, cipher, keyslots) and, where a key is supplied, open the volume. Reading metadata and opening through the device mapper are different runtime capabilities; opening needs facilities a worker may not have. No macOS install route is declared.

binaries.name: fvdeinfo
binaries.why: Read the encryption metadata of a Core Storage (legacy FileVault 2) volume and its key material references. Whether the installed build reads an APFS volume is not established; no macOS install route is declared.

binaries.name: john
binaries.why: Turn a header into a hash a password attempt can be made against, with the *2john helpers. Only where the operator has authorised it; no skill instructs its use. Whether a governed recovery capability exists is the owner's decision; apt's john and brew's john-jumbo are not shown to be the same feature set, and the *2john helpers are not checked here.

binaries.name: gpg
binaries.why: Read an OpenPGP message's packets (recipients, algorithms, the key it wants) with --list-packets before any key is known; use a key the case supplies, offline, in an isolated GNUPGHOME under $OUT with no keyring of the host and no secret on a command line.
